clue.text: Mails page going into review supplement

parts.note: to mail a letter is to post it

indicators.note: something going into another thing ends up sitting inside it

parts.note: crit is short for a critique or critical review
p is the standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: An office worker posts a page tucked inside a review's supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: A crit is art-school and theatre slang for a critique; the page sits just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A postscript is an addition tacked on after a letter or book is finished, so it is a kind of supplement.

clue.text: Ate cohoe's shirred egg-cases

indicators.note: shirred eggs are baked eggs, and shirring also means gathering fabric, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the 's

explanation.surface: Someone ate a salmon's baked eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: A cohoe is a coho, a Pacific salmon, which fits the egg picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Oothecae are the protective capsules some insects, like cockroaches, lay their eggs in, so they are egg-cases.

clue.text: Shrew like this dominates king

indicators.note: in a down entry, to dominate is to stand above, so the first piece goes on top

parts.note: so means in this way
rex is Latin for king, as on royal documents

explanation.surface: A nagging woman of this sort bosses her king about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrew' suggests a scolding wife, a picture that 'dominates king' supports; it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorex is the zoological genus of the common shrews, the small insect-eating mammals.

clue.text: Well over half of Lithuania is mined for this oxide

indicators.note: mined material is dug up and broken apart, so the letters come out jumbled
the phrase asks for a large opening share of the next word, more than half its length

parts.note: the first six of its nine letters

explanation.surface: Most of a Baltic country is dug up for a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Thulia is thulium oxide, a compound of the rare earth metal thulium with oxygen.

clue.text: Some of these dancers may be seen in US saloon

indicators.note: some of means only part of the run of letters that follows is wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Dancing girls might be watched in an American Wild West saloon bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' points to a bar; here it is a British word for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is the British term for a car with a fixed roof and separate boot; Americans call it a sedan.

clue.text: Gregory possibly using rail to span cracked axle

indicators.note: to span something is to stretch across both sides of it

parts.note: to rail against something is to rant

indicators.note: something cracked is broken, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Gregory uses a rail to bridge a broken axle.
explanation.walkthrough: Gregory is not a person but Gregory's powder, an old rhubarb-based laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregory's powder was a laxative, and a laxative is a relaxant of the bowels, so it is an example.

clue.text: Trouble in the waterworks? The old man admits year on bender!

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the following pieces go inside

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: on means placed in front of, in sequence with what follows

parts.note: y is the abbreviation for year
Uri Geller is famous for claiming to bend spoons

explanation.surface: Dad confesses a year-long drinking spree caused bladder trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bender' reads as a drinking binge; it is the spoon-bender. 'Waterworks' is jokey British slang for the urinary system.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyuria is pus in the urine, a medical sign of infection in the urinary system.

clue.text: Local chief to get (or give) a roasting

parts.note: taken as written
parch works both ways: to be scorched or to scorch something

explanation.surface: A town's leader either gives or gets a severe telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: A roasting looks like a scolding, but it is literal heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A toparch is the ruler of a small state or district, a governor of purely local power.

clue.text: Recognized king restored

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
something restored is made as good as new

explanation.surface: A monarch returned to the throne was identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' looks like a reversal or anagram signal, but it only supplies a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Knew is the past tense of know, which can mean to identify someone on sight, as recognized does.

clue.text: Grade maybe raised, typical of scholar — thoroughly deserved

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: Lew Grade was a British TV and film impresario, one Grade among others
learned means scholarly

explanation.surface: A student's grade, perhaps bumped up, was earned through scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grade' looks like an exam mark but is Lord Grade, the British television mogul; 'maybe' marks him as one of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-earned has been fully merited by effort, so it is thoroughly deserved.

clue.text: How smelly bits of putrid offal often hum!

definitions.text: How smelly bits of putrid offal often hum!

indicators.note: only small bits of each following word are wanted, here the opening letter of each

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A disgusted cook notes how rotten offal tends to stink.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the exclamation is exactly what you say on smelling such offal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooh is an interjection voicing disgust, typically at a bad smell, which is what the clue describes.

clue.text: Each evening whisky bottles getting drunk

parts.note: eve is a poetic word for evening

indicators.note: a bottle holds its contents, so this word holds the next idea inside it

parts.note: rye is a whisky distilled from rye grain
to be a bit on is colloquial for being tipsy

explanation.surface: Someone drinks whisky every evening and gets drunk each time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit on' is British slang for slightly drunk. 'Each' looks like part of the drinking routine, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Each, used as a pronoun for every person in a group, means the same as everyone.

clue.text: Sprinkling lustred pastry

indicators.note: sprinkling scatters things about, so the following letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker scatters glaze over a glossy pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a rolled layered pastry with a fruit filling, a well-known Austrian baked dessert.

clue.text: Lumpy leviathan charges yawl at sea, clipping yard

indicators.note: at sea means all confused, so the letters are in disorder
to clip something is to cut a piece off it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A sea monster attacks a small sailing boat out at sea, damaging its spar.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y of yawl is cut before the anagram. A yard is also a ship's spar, which the sailing scene suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrag whale is a grey whale with knobs instead of a dorsal fin along its back, hence lumpy.

clue.text: Overlay's taken up for one moveable hearth

indicators.note: 's here stands for has, and something that has taken another thing in now contains it

parts.note: a cel is a transparent sheet laid over a background in animation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sheet of overlay has been lifted off, as one might lift a portable fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' marks the definition as an example: a cupel is one kind of moveable hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupel is a small shallow vessel used as a portable hearth in assaying metals, so it is one instance of a moveable hearth.

clue.text: Bits of crab, each dressed with fringes of lettuce

indicators.note: dressing a crab means preparing and rearranging it, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the fringes of a word are its outermost edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dressed crab salad: each piece of crab garnished with lettuce edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelae are the pincer claws of crabs and lobsters, the plural of chela, so they are parts of a crab.

clue.text: On all fours, one's stomach gaining some momentum

parts.note: a means one, and the 's makes it possessive
a craw is a crop or stomach
L is the physics symbol for angular momentum, one kind of momentum

explanation.surface: Someone crawling on hands and knees gets their belly moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's stomach' reads as a single possessive phrase: A + CRAW. 'some momentum' is a hint that L is only one kind of momentum.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrawl is an adjective for crawling, so someone acrawl is moving about on hands and knees.

clue.text: Peg out after swallowing a restricted multi-part medicine

indicators.note: to swallow is to take something inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: to peg out is slang for to die
taken as written
pent means penned in or confined

explanation.surface: Someone dies after swallowing a dangerous prescription drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Diapente was an old medicine compounded from five ingredients, from the Greek for 'by five', so it has many parts.

clue.text: The old tend to compete about both ends of rug

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is put around the other

parts.note: to vie is to compete

indicators.note: both ends of a word are just its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Old people are inclined to fight over the edges of a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an obsolete form: virge is an old spelling of verge.
explanation.definitionFit: To verge is to incline or tend in a direction, and virge is its obsolete spelling, hence 'the old'.

clue.text: Fish? With a bit of dressing it would make one jealous

indicators.note: the answer is what is left once a letter is added back to make something else, so it lacks that letter

parts.note: green-eyed means jealous

indicators.note: a bit of a word means just one letter of it, here the opening one

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An angler wonders whether a fish, nicely garnished, would make a rival envious.
explanation.walkthrough: Add D to the fish and you get GREEN-EYED, the jealous look. The clue works backwards: the answer plus a letter makes the wordplay word.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeneye is a small deep-sea fish named for its large greenish eyes.

clue.text: Semitic language, one to preserve, Muslim beak penned

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: penned means shut inside an enclosure, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
a cadi is a judge in a Muslim country; beak is British slang for a magistrate

explanation.surface: A scholar of an ancient language works to protect a Muslim judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Accadian (Akkadian) is the ancient Semitic tongue of Assyria and Babylonia, written in cuneiform.

clue.text: Apple, brilliant as a stuffing for fish

indicators.note: a stuffing goes inside whatever it fills, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a familiar food fish
star as an adjective means outstanding or brilliant

explanation.surface: A recipe recommending apple as a stuffing for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A costard is a large old English variety of cooking apple, which gave costermonger its name.

clue.text: Knock up finial with splayed ends

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: to tap is to knock lightly
a tee is the umbrella-shaped finial topping a pagoda

explanation.surface: Fix a decorative top piece whose ends flare outwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock up' looks like one phrasal verb, but 'up' only turns the knock around.
explanation.definitionFit: Pattée describes a heraldic cross whose arms widen towards their tips, so its ends are splayed.

clue.text: Silence in ghastly ravine — one just disappears

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second
something ghastly is a horrible mess, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
sh is the sound you make to call for silence

explanation.surface: In the hush of a frightening gorge, someone simply vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vanisher is a person or thing that vanishes, that is, simply disappears from view.

clue.text: Stuff trained dogs eat (not heart)

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is to be left out
trained means drilled into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the word without its middle letter

explanation.surface: A recipe for food that performing dogs might eat, filling but heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: To stodge is to cram or stuff oneself with food, and stodge is heavy filling food.

clue.text: Little succeeded in feeble Buddhist festival

indicators.note: in sets the first piece inside the second

parts.note: feeble means weak
s, written small, is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A frail celebration barely managed to come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals the lower-case s used in genealogies.
explanation.definitionFit: Wesak, or Vesak, is the Buddhist festival marking the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death, held in May.

clue.text: Adorn part of kisser dolled up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom
part of means only some of the run of letters is wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A woman makes up her face for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dolled up' looks like one phrase meaning dressed up; 'up' is the reversal signal. 'Kisser' is slang for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress something is to decorate it, as with dressing a shop window, so it means adorn.

clue.text: Nasty little nipper holding end of tall javelin

indicators.note: something holding another keeps it inside

parts.note: a pium is a small biting fly of Brazil

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A spiteful child grabs the tip of a tall spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' suggests a child but is a biting insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilum was the heavy throwing spear carried by Roman legionaries, a form of javelin.

clue.text: Object of lust, excessive, gripped by urge

indicators.note: something gripped by another is held inside it

parts.note: hie is an old verb meaning to urge on or hasten
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: Someone describes an overpowering urge for the object of their desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hottie is slang for a sexually attractive person, the kind of person who becomes an object of lust.

clue.text: Tanker line yielding bit of cash for old Greek

definitions.text: bit of cash for old Greek

parts.note: an OBO is an ore-bulk-oil carrier, a ship that can serve as a tanker
l is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A shipping line's tanker earns a little money for a Greek owner.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, worth a sixth of a drachma.

clue.text: Lop old old homily around middle of benediction

indicators.note: around puts the first piece on both sides of the second

parts.note: prone is an obsolete word for a sermon or homily

indicators.note: only the central letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the central letter of this ten-letter word, its sixth

explanation.surface: A cut-down sermon on blessings, shortened by an old preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'old's are not a misprint: one marks the archaic definition, the other the archaic homily.
explanation.definitionFit: Proine is an obsolete form of prune, to lop branches off a tree, hence 'old'.

clue.text: To reduce muscle, tucked in

parts.note: ab is short for an abdominal muscle
to tuck in is to eat heartily

explanation.surface: Advice that trimming your muscle means pulling it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked in' looks like a container signal, but it is past-tense eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate something is to lessen it, a direct synonym of reduce.

clue.text: State requiring relief with leader being heckled

parts.note: need is the condition of wanting help
led means guided, having had a leader

explanation.surface: A country in crisis has its president jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or goad them, much as hecklers keep taunting a speaker.

clue.text: Prostitutes of old, look, roaming street

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reminder that streetwalkers of the past roamed the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorettes were kept women or courtesans in 19th-century Paris, named after a district church.

clue.text: Antique dress, by the sound of it, accompaniment for dolls?

indicators.note: the phrase asks us to judge a word by how it is said, not how it is spelt

parts.note: guise in its old sense means dress or costume

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned clothes for dolls, with something to go with them.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the musical Guys and Dolls, where guys accompany the dolls.
explanation.definitionFit: In the title of the musical Guys and Dolls, guys go along with dolls, so they are their companions.

clue.text: Canadian backs (say) in private room ingesting iron and bodily fluid

indicators.note: ingesting means taking something inside, so one piece is swallowed by another

parts.note: a den is a private room or study
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
one of the body's fluids

explanation.surface: An odd scene of a Canadian swallowing iron and body fluid in his den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canadian' explains the spelling with S; '(say)' marks backs as an example, ice hockey players in defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Defensemen are the ice hockey players who play at the back, the North American spelling of defencemen.
